findings.message: D9 makes `anchor id` part of the obligation id, but D2 explicitly says obligations are derived per entry and are not multiplied by cite count. Downstream derivation cannot know whether to emit one obligation per declaration item, reusing its test group across all cited anchors, or one obligation per `(entry, anchor, kind, item)`. That changes obligation counts, binding shape, and totality semantics, so the ADR needs one consistent identity model before spec/types can translate it.

D14 classifies `sotp test-obligation results` as part of the fail-closed gate, but the same decision later says it is informational, always exits 0, and that `check` alone owns pass/fail. That makes the ADR internally inconsistent on whether `results` is a gate or a viewer, so downstream CLI/spec implementers cannot derive one observable contract.
findings.category: inconsistent decisions within the same ADR

findings.message: D14 adds `sotp test-obligation bindings-skeleton` as another subcommand in the same `sotp test-obligation` group, but D11 still states that this group has exactly four subcommands. D14 later says the helper is not part of D11's four commands, yet it is still a same-group CLI subcommand, so downstream spec/type planning cannot tell whether the CLI surface is four commands or five with four gate commands plus one authoring helper. Update D11/D14 to consistently distinguish the four gate subcommands from the non-gate helper.

findings.message: D15 は follow-up track まで実装延期される決定ですが、本文にはその適用時期が明記されていません。むしろ「D15 により…コミットが可能」「自動的に 🔵 必須のレーンに切り替わる」など、現行 `check` が既に task-status-aware であるように読めます。下流 spec と運用が未実装の挙動を現行契約として扱わないよう、決定は記録済みだが実装は後続 track に延期され、それまでは従来の status-blind 判定が継続する旨を明記してください。

D15 は後続 track が merge されるまで `check` が status-blind のままだと定めていますが、D16 は fingerprint 不一致時の `check` が「D15 の task-status レーンによる最終解釈を含む」と現在形で記述しています。これでは下流 spec が、D16 導入時点から todo を 🟡 扱いするのか、D15 導入までは全件 block するのかを一意に導出できません。「D15 導入後は」など適用時期を明記してください。

「決定表の欠陥」を無条件に非ブロッカーとしていますが、直前では role 欠落などの構造的欠陥を `derive` / `check` が fail-closed で阻止すると決定しており、D4 も非ブロッカー対象を内容レベルに限定しています。CN-12 の下流契約が構造的欠陥まで通過可能と誤読されないよう、「内容レベルの欠陥・調整不足」に限定し、構造的破綻は引き続き block する旨を明記してください。

findings.message: The Summary block restates the upstream design intent for the whole track in prose instead of keeping the text to target + operation + anchor cite.

S6 restates the derive/check/evaluate/results contracts in prose, including deterministic projection, totality, cache freezing, and aggregation semantics.
S7 restates the CLI wiring contract in prose; T020-T022 should be trimmed to target + operation + anchor cite.
S8 restates the capability-registration contract in prose instead of keeping the section to the executable change description.

S5 (T014-T015) restates verifier prompt semantics and fail-category behavior (`required supporting quotations`, `three-fail-type discrimination`, `edge-local self-containment`) in the task text; that belongs in the spec, not the impl-plan wording.

S6 (T016-T019) embeds the derive/check/evaluate/results behavioral contract (`Deterministic projection`, `Pure-read totality gate`, `always returns success outcome`, cache/traversal semantics) directly in task prose, which is upstream restatement.
T022 restates CLI behavior and exit semantics (`No --lenient / --force / --context / --layer / --scope flags`, `results exit is always 0`) instead of staying at target + operation + anchor cite.
T023 restates capability-routing behavior (`fast → final escalation resolves per capability`) rather than just naming the config/registry edits and anchor cite.

T009's contract overstates the task text: it attributes `SemanticVerifierError`, `ArtifactCodecError`, `TestSourceScanError`, and `VerifyCacheError`, but the task description only names `ObligationCheckError`, `ObligationDeriveError`, `ObligationEvaluateError`, `ObligationResultsError`, `FulfillmentFailCategory`, and the port types. Either expand the task description to cover those entries or remove them from the contract.

T020's task-contract attributes `TestObligationDeriveInput`, `TestObligationCheckInput`, `TestObligationEvaluateInput`, and `TestObligationResultsInput`, but the T020 task description only names the four handler types and does not claim to add or modify these input entries. T022's task-contract omits `TestObligationResultsArgs` even though the T022 task description explicitly lists `TestObligationResultsArgs` among the CLI args to add. That leaves a catalogue entry claimed by the task without task-contract attribution.

`AC-16` is mapped to `T014`, but `T014` only targets `test_obligation::fulfillment_verifier` provider wiring and its cited anchors are `IN-09/IN-12/CN-03/CN-08/AC-06/AC-08/OS-01`; it does not touch `trait_impls`, `contract_conformance`, or trait-edge evidence selection. This makes the `AC-16` coverage assignment implausible and misassigns load-bearing fulfillment-evaluation work away from the tasks that actually describe it.

`AC-11` is mapped to `T015`, but `T015` only adds the `WaiverVerifierAdapter` provider wiring. It does not target waiver-fail routing, preserving obligations without verifier-injected additions, or routing-brief handling, which are the load-bearing parts of `AC-11`; those are usecase/evaluate responsibilities already described by `T018`.

AC-12 is mapped to T016 and T017, but those task descriptions do not cite AC-12 or describe the derive/check work needed for voluntary bindings; only T018 carries the AC-12 cite. That makes the coverage mapping implausible for the derive/check portions of AC-12's transition path.

T004 restates upstream behavior in prose: `load-time totality verification and per-axis vocabulary parsing` plus the named fail cases duplicate AC-02/CN-05 details. Per `knowledge/conventions/no-upstream-restatement.md`, this should be target + operation + anchor cite only.

`JsonTestObligationRulesLoader::load` reads `config_path` with `read_to_string` but never rejects symlinks. That means a symlinked `test-obligation-rules.json` will be followed to its target instead of enforcing real-file semantics, unlike the other config loaders in this repo that `symlink_metadata()` and fail closed before reading.

This guard only rejects symlinks; it never canonicalizes or verifies that `config_path` stays within a fixed trusted root. A non-symlink path with `..` components can therefore escape the expected `.harness/config` boundary and be read directly. The existing `scope_config_loader.rs` pattern canonicalizes the root/path and `starts_with`-checks containment before reading.

`JsonTestObligationRulesLoader` does not anchor its trust boundary to an external `trusted_root`. When `.harness/config` is absent, `infer_symlink_trusted_root` and `infer_config_boundary_root` both fall back to `config_path.parent()`, so the containment check at `guard_config_path` becomes tautological and the adapter will read arbitrary files or files under a symlinked directory if the leaf itself is not a symlink. This is a trusted-root violation; compare the explicit `trusted_root` + canonicalize pattern used by `load_v2_scope_config` in `review_v2/scope_config_loader.rs`.

`reject_symlinks_below` treats its second argument as an already-trusted root and does not stat it. This codec passes `items_dir` as that root without first rejecting a symlinked `items_dir`, so constructing the adapter with `track/items` as a symlink lets `load` read through the symlink and `save` create/write under the symlink target outside the intended workspace boundary. Mirror the existing trusted-root pattern by checking the root itself before using it as the guard root.

`reject_symlinks_below` assumes `items_dir` is already a safe trusted root, but this adapter never checks that root. A symlinked `items_dir` is therefore accepted, and the subsequent `read_to_string`/`write` operations follow it outside the intended artifact tree. Reject a symlinked root before joining track artifacts beneath it.

The fulfillment cache guard checks components below `items_dir`, but not `items_dir` itself. Because `read_to_string` and `write` follow symlinks, a symlinked cache root can redirect cache I/O outside the trusted track items directory. Add an explicit root symlink rejection before using `items_dir` as the guard root.

The waiver cache adapter uses `items_dir` as the trusted root for `reject_symlinks_below` without validating that root. If `items_dir` is a symlink, the guard stops before inspecting it and the cache load/save follows the symlink target, violating the real-file boundary convention. Reject symlinked roots before artifact path resolution.

`location.module_path()` is split into `crate_name`/`rest` and both are concatenated into `workspace_root/...` with `join`/`push` but no containment check against `workspace_root`. A crafted module path containing `..` or an absolute component can escape the worktree before `read_to_string` runs.

`std::fs::read_to_string(&file)` will follow symlinks, but this scanner never does a `symlink_metadata()`/reject check on candidate files or the workspace root. That means a symlinked test source under the worktree is accepted instead of being fail-closed.

`guarded_workspace_root()` canonicalizes the caller-supplied workspace root after only checking the final path component for symlinks. That can follow symlinked ancestor components and re-anchor the scanner on the target tree, which violates the trusted-root boundary. The existing `verify/trusted_root.rs` pattern keeps the root lexical and only rejects a symlinked root instead of calling `canonicalize()` here.

`guarded_workspace_root()` only `symlink_metadata()`-checks the leaf `workspace_root` path. If the repo is reached through a symlinked parent such as `/tmp/link/repo`, this passes, and the later `reject_symlinks_below()` calls treat that untrusted anchor as the trusted root. That leaves the scanner able to read from a redirected tree instead of rejecting the symlink boundary, which is the case the trusted-root / symlink-guard precedent in `verify/trusted_root.rs` is meant to block.

`read_track_metadata` and `load_impl_plan_for_track` still call `std::fs::read_to_string` on `items_dir.join(id)` paths without the `symlink_metadata` / `reject_symlinks_below` guard that `read_track_status_str` applies. A symlinked `items_dir` or track directory will be followed and can read outside the trusted root, so these public helpers do not fail closed at the filesystem boundary.

`guarded_items_dir()` canonicalizes `items_dir` lexically before any containment check, so a path like `.../link/../items` can hide a symlinked component from `reject_symlinked_items_dir_chain()` and be re-anchored outside the intended track tree. `read_track_metadata()` / `load_impl_plan_for_track()` then trust that escaped directory as the root; this needs the same fail-closed `ParentDir`/containment guard used by the existing symlink-safe loaders.

`FsTrackStore` still builds primary port paths with raw `self.root.join(...).join(...)` and then calls `path.exists()`/`std::fs::read_to_string` without rejecting symlinks. `ImplPlanReader::load_impl_plan` repeats the same pattern for `impl-plan.json`, so callers of `TrackReader::find` / `ImplPlanReader::load_impl_plan` can follow a symlinked track directory or leaf file under the configured items root. Route these reads through the same trusted-root and `reject_symlinks_below` guard used by `read_track_metadata` / `guarded_track_file_path`.

`save_impl_plan` still builds the write target with `self.root.join(id.as_ref()).join("impl-plan.json")` and writes via `atomic_write_file` without first applying the same trusted-root/symlink guard used by the read paths. A symlinked `items_dir` or track directory can therefore redirect the impl-plan write outside the intended track-items root; this should fail closed via the existing `guarded_items_dir`/`reject_symlinks_below` pattern before creating the parent or temp file.

`with_locked_document` derives `metadata.json.lock` from a guarded metadata path, but then opens the lock with `std::fs::File::create` without checking the lock path itself for symlinks. A pre-existing symlink at `<track>/metadata.json.lock` will be followed and truncated before the lock is taken, bypassing the symlink-rejection boundary used elsewhere and conflicting with the scope_config_loader.rs symlink-rejection precedent. Guard `lock_path` with `reject_symlinks_below` or equivalent no-follow semantics before creating it.

`FsSpecDocumentLoader::load` reads `spec.json` with `std::fs::read_to_string` directly, so a symlinked leaf or ancestor is followed instead of being rejected at the filesystem boundary. That lets workspace-controlled `spec.json` paths escape the trusted root and diverges from the repo's established `reject_symlinks_below` pattern used for config loaders such as `review_v2/scope_config_loader.rs` before reading. Add an explicit symlink guard before the read.

P1: `FsSpecDocumentLoader` does not have a real trusted root. In `reject_spec_path_symlinks()` it derives `trusted_root` from `spec_path.ancestors().last()` ([`document_loader.rs`](<machine-home>/individual/t-rust/templates/SoTOHE-core-002/libs/infrastructure/src/spec/document_loader.rs#L54)), which is `""` for relative paths and the filesystem root for absolute paths. That means the loader will accept caller-supplied `../...` paths and can read outside the workspace as long as the path is not a symlink. Thread the workspace/items root into the adapter and reject paths that are not contained under it before calling `read_to_string`.

`FsSpecDocumentLoader` only rejects a symlink at the `trusted_root` leaf and below it. Because `reject_symlinks_below` treats the anchor as trusted, a symlink in any ancestor of `trusted_root` is still followed, so a caller that passes a symlinked workspace/items root can read `spec.json` outside the intended boundary. This needs a root-level real-path check before the descendant walk.

The path guard normalizes `trusted_root` and `spec_path` before any symlink inspection. A path such as `<trusted_root>/link/../spec.json` can lose the symlinked `link` component during `lexical_normalize`, so `reject_symlinked_trusted_root` and `reject_symlinks_below` never see the traversal. That breaks the trusted-root boundary and can admit reads outside the intended root.

`std::thread::spawn` panics when the OS cannot create a worker thread, so resource exhaustion terminates this library path instead of returning the verifier's typed error. Additionally, if `thunk()` panics, no result is stored or waker fired and the evaluation future remains pending indefinitely. Use `std::thread::Builder::spawn` and propagate both spawn and worker failures through the future's result type.

All 75 `target_entry.file_path` values embed this reviewer's absolute checkout path. These committed artifacts are therefore non-portable: in another checkout, declaration lookup cannot match the current catalogue paths, causing declaration hashes and frozen cache verdicts to become stale and the commit gate to fail. Store project-relative catalogue paths instead.

The refreshed fulfilled verdict for WaiverVerifierPort × IN-09 cites only `ObligationFulfillmentVerifierAdapter::render_prompt`. That test exercises the other verifier and provides no evidence that waiver claims are evaluated or that WaiverVerifierPort preserves the waiver-specific behavior promised by IN-09. Re-freeze this entry using waiver-verifier evidence.

The amended IN-11 covers both profile-load failure and a successfully loaded profile whose capability cannot be resolved, but the added composition-root binding only tests the first case; the other bound test is a happy path. Consequently this record can be marked fulfilled without evidence that the composition root wires distinct stand-ins for unresolvable capabilities. Add and bind a composition-root test using a valid profile missing each capability, then refresh the cache.

AC-04 defines the complete pass condition as resolved edges with current-hash verdicts, but the newly expanded IN-08 additionally requires `obligations.json` to equal the in-memory re-derived obligation set. A stale artifact can satisfy AC-04 while IN-08 requires failure, leaving the behavioral contract contradictory and the new requirement without an acceptance check. Update AC-04 so stale added, removed, and changed obligations must deterministically produce a nonzero exit while preserving pure-read behavior.

`SemanticEscalationDriverPort` is the shared escalation/cache port for concurrent semantic evaluation, but the trait leaves `P`, `K`, `V`, `E`, and the future produced by the public `async fn` unconstrained. A non-`Send`/non-`Sync` implementation can satisfy this usecase port, so later ref-verify or obligation-gate orchestration cannot safely fan out evaluations across workers despite the port contract being the concurrency boundary. Add the required `Send`/`Sync` bounds and use a `Send` future shape at the trait boundary instead of an unconstrained public `async fn`.
findings.category: purity violation by trait or generic

findings.message: This usecase re-parses raw `spec.json` locally instead of consuming the parsed `SpecDocument` boundary. That duplicates codec/schema logic in `check` and can drift from the canonical parser used elsewhere for uncited AC/CN detection.

`current_bound_hash` here, and the same helper pattern in `evaluate.rs`, drop `TestSourceScanError`s and hash only the bodies that happened to load. A missing or unreadable test source therefore looks like a successful binding over partial evidence, so freshness checks can proceed on incomplete data.

In `execute`, catalogue / obligations / bindings / spec load failures are all returned as `CacheWrite`. That public error type says persistence failed even when the actual failure was reading inputs, so callers get the wrong remediation path.

When both obligations and bindings are absent, `execute` returns before rewriting the verdict caches. That leaves any previously materialized fulfillment/waiver cache files on disk, so a later `results` run can report stale verdicts for an empty scope.

`detect_orphaned` only inspects `TestBindingRecord::Fulfillment`. Waiver bindings that survive after their edge is no longer derived are never marked orphaned, because `resolve_edges` only walks current obligations. That lets stale waiver records slip through a clean `check` run.

`WaiverVerdict::Fail` is recorded as `EdgeResolutionOutcome::MissingBinding`. That misclassifies a rejected waiver as an absent binding, so the results output cannot distinguish the two failure modes.

`trait_impl` obligations are emitted with an empty anchor list. Both downstream gates derive edges exclusively from `obligation.spec_refs()`, and `evaluate_record` only calls the verifier inside that anchor loop, so a bound contract-conformance obligation can produce zero verifier calls/cache entries and still avoid unresolved-edge handling. This drops required trait-impl conformance coverage instead of resolving the implemented trait's spec anchors as the module comment describes.

Fresh evaluation always calls the semantic verifier and overwrites cache entries without first loading/reusing an existing verdict whose three-hash key already matches. That breaks the frozen-cache contract: rerunning `evaluate` on unchanged inputs can replace a previously passing final verdict with a new fail/pending result from the external verifier, making the gate non-deterministic and defeating drift-based cache invalidation.

`resolve_fulfillment_edge` selects a fulfillment cache entry by `edge_id` only, but fulfillment cache entries are keyed by both `edge_id` and `obligation_id`. Since an edge is only `(entry_key, anchor)`, multiple obligations for the same entry/anchor can share it; a fulfilled verdict for one obligation can therefore satisfy another obligation without its own verifier verdict if the hashes line up. Match the cache entry on the current `obligation.id()` as well before marking the edge resolved.

Trait-impl obligations use `impl_decl.for_type` as the obligation entry key while freezing the declaration hash from the `impl_decl` itself. Later evaluate/check resolve declarations only by that entry key through types/traits/functions, so a trait-impl obligation either gets the adapter type declaration or no declaration, not the impl declaration that was hashed. This makes trait-impl verification go pending or produce permanent `decl_changed` drift. Carry a resolvable trait-impl target/declaration, or teach declaration lookup to find the matching `trait_impls` declaration with the same canonical text.

Fulfillment evaluation resolves the current catalogue declaration text, but freezes and cache-matches the verdict with the stale `obligation.declaration_hash()` from the obligations artifact. If the catalogue declaration changes without changing the obligation id, `evaluate` can reuse an old cached verdict without re-verifying the new declaration, or write a cache entry that `check` immediately reports as `decl_changed`. The fulfillment key should hash the resolved `declaration` used for `verify_pair`, as the voluntary and waiver paths already do.

Waiver evaluation and freshness checking resolve declaration text from only `edge.entry_key()`. For trait-impl obligations the edge key is the implementer type, while the correct declaration is the specific `TraitImplDeclV2` identified by `trait_impl:<trait>` on the obligation. A waived trait-impl edge is therefore verified and cache-checked against the type declaration instead of the impl declaration, so changes to the impl can be missed and the verifier receives the wrong evidence.

P1: `EvaluateTestObligationsInteractor` bypasses the shared semantic escalation core. The implementation hard-codes `fast -> final` by calling the verifier ports directly and never injects or calls `SemanticEscalationDriverPort`; as a result the configured calibration-probe injection, degradation threshold, parallelism, and human-escalation path required for the obligation gate are skipped, with final fail/pending verdicts merely cached and returned in an `Ok` outcome.

`execute` only fails closed when `pending_records` is populated, but these unresolved-input branches only increment `tally.pending` and return `Ok(())`. A binding that references a missing obligation, missing declaration, or missing spec anchor therefore lets `evaluate` complete successfully with `pending_count > 0` and no human-escalation error, silently bypassing the fail-closed evaluation gate. Record a pending `EdgeVerdictRecord` or return a typed error for these resolution failures.

`derive_trait_impl_obligations` resolves trait impls by passing the raw `trait_ref` through `simplify_trait_ref`, which strips both generics and all path qualifiers before matching against catalogue trait names. That means an external impl like `std::fmt::Display` will be treated as the local catalogue trait `Display` whenever one exists, so the code emits contract-conformance obligations instead of the required zero-obligation external-trait case. This is a usecase-level string decision on `TypeRef` identity that should be handled by the domain/catalogue resolution model, and it breaks IN-17/AC-16 for same-basename external traits.

`block_on` is a production usecase executor that repeatedly polls a `SemanticEscalationFuture` with a noop waker and spins on `Poll::Pending`. The `SemanticEscalationDriverPort` contract returns `Send` futures for worker fan-out; it does not promise ready-only futures, so this makes the usecase layer depend on an implicit runtime behavior and can hang the evaluate gate when a real async verifier adapter yields. Move future execution to the composition/runtime boundary, make this service async, or make the verifier port synchronous if usecase must stay sync.
findings.category: purity violation by trait or generic

findings.message: The new interactors store injected dependencies as bare `Arc<dyn ...>` trait objects, starting here with `rules_loader`; the same pattern appears in check/evaluate/results. The briefing requires injected Arc ports to be `Send + Sync`, and without those bounds a non-thread-safe infrastructure adapter can be wired into the usecase orchestrator, breaking the expected port contract and preventing safe sharing/fan-out of the application services. Add `+ Send + Sync` to the injected trait objects, or make the port traits themselves require those bounds.
findings.category: purity violation by trait or generic

findings.message: `input_load_error` wraps every read-side failure as `ObligationEvaluateError::CachePersistence(VerifyCacheError::Io(...))`, and it is used for catalogue loads, spec loads, and test-source scans, not just cache persistence. That re-exposes an infrastructure-shaped IO/cache error through the usecase API and collapses unrelated evaluation input failures into a cache error, so callers cannot route the failure at the usecase concept level. Add usecase-level input/source/artifact error variants or map these failures to existing non-cache concepts instead.

P1 error type confusion: `input_load_error` maps catalogue loads, spec loads, obligation/binding artifact loads, and test-source scan failures into `ObligationEvaluateError::CachePersistence(VerifyCacheError::Io(...))`. That means callers see non-cache input failures as verdict-cache I/O failures, which breaks the usecase error abstraction required by the usecase severity policy. Add usecase-level evaluate error variants for input/artifact/source/spec failures, or map each port failure to the existing conceptually correct variant instead of the cache persistence lane.

P1 error type confusion: catalogue and spec document loader failures are collapsed into `ObligationCheckError::ArtifactCodec(ArtifactCodecError::Io(...))`, even though `ArtifactCodecError` is documented for obligations/test-bindings artifacts and `SpecDocumentLoadError` distinguishes not-found, I/O, JSON parse, and invariant failures. This makes check callers report spec/catalogue input failures as generic artifact I/O and loses the usecase-level failure concept. Map these ports to dedicated check error variants or a non-artifact input-load error.

The derive interactor parses `TraitImplDeclV2.trait_ref` as a raw string to decide whether an impl targets a local trait (`split('<')` plus `contains("::")`). That is domain classification logic for the `TypeRef`/catalogue model, not usecase orchestration; if the domain encoding changes, the usecase can silently skip or emit obligations incorrectly. Move this behind a domain method/value-type API and have the interactor call that.

`SpecDocumentLoaderPort` is defined in the usecase layer even though it abstracts loading/parsing the persisted `SpecDocument` artifact, i.e. a domain document persistence boundary. Per `knowledge/conventions/hexagonal-architecture.md` §Port Placement Rules, ports for persistence/domain concepts belong in `domain` (as with the existing `CatalogueDocumentLoaderPort`), while usecase should only depend on them. Keeping this port here also forces `domain` to carry `SpecDocumentLoadError` for a usecase-owned trait. Move the port next to the spec domain types/error and inject that domain port into derive/check/evaluate.

The derive interactor is making domain role decisions in the usecase layer: `data_role_items` and the helpers it dispatches to match on `DataRole`/`TypeKindV2` to decide which invariants, handles, events, typestate transitions, and methods produce obligation items. Per `hexagonal-architecture.md` §CLI as Composition Root / usecase purity, the usecase layer should orchestrate loaded catalogues/rules and delegate these domain-role semantics to domain types or a domain projector; otherwise role semantic changes can drift independently in usecase.

`TestObligationResultsInteractor` maps both `ObligationsArtifactPort::load` and `TestBindingsArtifactPort::load` failures to `MalformedArtifact`, so a plain I/O failure is reported as corruption and the `IoError` branch on `ObligationResultsError` is never used here. Callers lose the retry-vs-corruption distinction for results loading.

Workspace-qualified trait refs lose their `crate_name` here: `TraitRefScope::Workspace { crate_name, bare_name }` is collapsed to `bare_name`, then the first catalogue entry with that name wins. If two workspace crates expose the same trait name, `impl usecase::Foo for Bar` can be projected against the wrong role/anchors depending on catalogue order.

`cited_anchor_ids()` treats deletion tombstones as active citations because it walks `iter_catalogue_entries()` without checking `entry.action`. That means an `AC`/`CN` requirement cited only by a deleted catalogue entry will be suppressed instead of being reported as uncited. Filter out `ItemAction::Delete` entries here (or in the traversal helper) before building the cited set.

This branch maps `scan_test_body() == Ok(None)` to `TestSourceScanError::Parse`, but the scanner contract uses `None` for an absent test/file, not a parse failure. That misclassifies missing source as malformed source and makes `check`'s error surface inconsistent with `evaluate`, which treats the same condition as I/O-style absence. Map the `None` case to an absence/I-O path instead of `Parse`.

Declaration lookup is keyed only by the bare entry name. If a type, trait, or function shares that name in another section, `find_declaration_text` can return the wrong declaration, so `check`/`evaluate` will freeze or verify against the wrong AST and report stale/fresh results incorrectly. The existing `CatalogueEntryRef.section_key` should be used to disambiguate.

`save_caches` writes the fulfillment cache before the waiver cache. If the second save fails, `evaluate` returns `Err` after mutating only one artifact, leaving the pair out of sync and allowing later `check`/`results` runs to observe a mixed-generation state. The cache writes need to be atomic or rolled back on failure.

Voluntary bindings never migrate onto a newly derived obligation. `check` ignores `TestBindingRecord::VoluntaryBinding` when it looks for fulfillment bindings, and `evaluate` keeps freezing those records under a synthetic obligation id instead of resolving an existing obligation for the same edge. That breaks AC-12 inheritance: after a decision-table update creates a real obligation, the old voluntary binding is still reported as missing / workspace-only instead of counting as that obligation's fulfillment.

`derive_trait_impl_obligations` bypasses the domain `RoleObligationItemsProjector` for trait-impl rules by ignoring the rule's `per_axis` and always returning one `trait_impl:<trait>` item. Because `TestObligationRulesDocument` accepts arbitrary `TestObligationPerAxis` values in the `trait_impls` section, a config using `per: "method"` or another non-`trait_impl` axis would still generate contract-conformance obligations instead of projecting zero/failing through the domain rule interpreter. This keeps role/per-axis business projection logic in the usecase layer and can derive obligations the domain projector would not authorize.

`execute_inner` treats a half-materialised scope as a clean zero-pair run: if either `obligations` or `bindings` is `None`, it clears both verdict caches and returns `Ok(0, 0, 0)`. That silently masks a missing artifact instead of surfacing the incomplete scope.

`libs/usecase/src/ref_verify/interactor.rs:272-301` now finalizes fast non-pass production pairs inside `RefVerifierEscalationDriver`, then immediately re-runs the same pairs through `parallel_verify(..., ModelTier::Final, ...)` in the calibration-failure branch. That doubles Final-tier verifier calls for every fast Fail/Pending pair, so a transient second-call error or any side effect on the verifier can make this branch fail where the previous single Final evaluation would not.

The per-category calibration gate credits a probe as detected whenever the verifier returns any `Fail`, then records the expected probe shape's category instead of checking the verdict's reported `category`. A verifier that labels every known-bad probe as `Contradiction` would still mark the substitution and central-unverified slots as detected, so AC-08's requirement that each failure shape be detected as its corresponding category is not enforced. The existing test default `fulfillment_fail()` always returns `CentralUnverified`, which masks this because all three issued categories still pass the tally. Match `ObligationFulfillmentVerdict::Fail { category, .. }` against `shape.category` before calling `record_detected`, and add a regression test for wrong-category failures.

Waiver provenance matches obligations by catalogue entry key alone. Valid documents may contain multiple obligations for one entry, or an edge whose anchor belongs to none of them, so this can attach an unrelated obligation ID instead of leaving it unresolved. Resolve ownership using the complete edge (including anchor membership) through domain-owned logic, consistent with `hexagonal-architecture.md` §CLI as Composition Root.

The waiver claim source is always populated as `"waiver"`, even when the bindings artifact is absent or contains no matching waiver record. That fabricates provenance for stale/orphaned cache entries; derive both claim and evidence from an exact binding match and leave them `None` when unresolved.

Waiver ownership is now matched correctly by entry key and anchor, but the ownership invariant is still implemented in the usecase layer. Selecting a unique obligation owner is a domain decision, not orchestration; move this resolution behind a domain-owned method (for example on `ObligationsDocument`) and have `results` consume its result, per `hexagonal-architecture.md` §CLI as Composition Root.

`stale_obligations_artifact_detail` implements the domain decision for whether two obligation documents are equivalent inside the usecase layer, contrary to `hexagonal-architecture.md` §CLI as Composition Root. The hand-written comparison is also incomplete: obligations with the same ID, declaration hash, and spec refs but different `target_entry`, `target_role`, or `brief`, as well as duplicate obligations, can pass as current. Move this equivalence/staleness rule onto the domain document and compare the complete obligation multiset.

`canonical_target_role` は `TargetEntryRoleKind` の各 variant を分岐し、ペイロードを捨てて永続化時の正規形へ変換しています。これはドメイン型の同値性・正規化を決めるビジネスロジックであり、純粋なオーケストレーターである usecase に置くべきではありません（`hexagonal-architecture.md` §Usecase Layer Purity Rules / §CLI as Composition Root）。`TargetEntryRoleKind` または各 role 型の domain メソッドへ移し、usecase はそのメソッドを呼び出すだけにしてください。

`domain::tddd::test_obligation::ports::ObligationsArtifactPort` and `TestBindingsArtifactPort` expose `load`/`save` with `ObligationCheckError` / `ObligationDeriveError`, but these codec boundaries can only surface I/O / JSON / invariant failures. Variants such as `RulesLoad`, `CatalogueLoad`, `SpecLoad`, `InvalidCatalogueState`, `ObligationsAbsent`, `BindingsAbsent`, `PartialArtifactState`, `DriftsDetected`, `UnresolvedEdges`, and `StaleVerdicts` are not constructible at the port layer.

`domain::tddd::test_obligation::ports::ObligationFulfillmentCachePort`, `WaiverCachePort`, `ObligationFulfillmentVerifierPort`, and `WaiverVerifierPort` all return `ObligationEvaluateError`, but the adapters behind those methods can only produce a narrow subset (`CachePersistence` for cache I/O, `VerifierPortError` for the LLM ports). Control-plane variants like `InvalidConfig`, `TrackNotActive`, `SemanticFailuresConfirmed`, and `HumanEscalationRequired` are not reachable from those methods.

`domain::tddd::test_obligation::ports::TestSourceScannerPort::scan_test_body` returns `ObligationCheckError`, but the scanner can only fail on I/O / parse / missing-test conditions. Higher-level check outcomes such as `ObligationsAbsent`, `BindingsAbsent`, `PartialArtifactState`, `DriftsDetected`, `UnresolvedEdges`, and `StaleVerdicts` are not constructible from that boundary.

Ownership smell: `ObligationFulfillmentVerifierPort::verify_pair` takes `tests_source`, `entry_declaration`, and `anchor_text` as owned `String`s even though the port is read-only and could borrow `&str`; this forces avoidable allocation/cloning at the usecase boundary.

Ownership smell: `WaiverVerifierPort::verify_pair` takes `waived_reason`, `entry_declaration`, and `anchor_text` as owned `String`s even though the port is read-only and could borrow `&str`; this forces avoidable allocation/cloning at the usecase boundary.

Lossy boundary downgrade: `ObligationCheckError::DriftsDetected`, `UnresolvedEdges`, and `StaleVerdicts` collapse structured failure data into counts, while `CheckTestObligationsOutcome` already carries the full `Vec<TestObligationDrift>`, `Vec<TestObligationEdgeId>`, and `Vec<UncitedSpecElementFinding>`; the error shape drops actionable detail without justification.

`test_obligation::evaluate::TestObligationEvaluateConfig::try_new` returns `ObligationEvaluateError`, but this constructor can only reject invalid config values. Callers still have to handle `TrackNotActive`, `VerifierPort`, `CachePersistence`, `SemanticFailuresConfirmed`, and `HumanEscalationRequired`, none of which are reachable at this boundary. Narrow the error type or document why the full enum is intentional.

`semantic_verdict_core::driver::SemanticEscalationDriverPort::evaluate_with_escalation` also returns `ObligationEvaluateError`, but the method only takes `key` and `initial_tier`. The config-only and track-only variants (`InvalidConfig`, `TrackNotActive`) are not structurally reachable here, so the shared error enum is broader than the port boundary warrants unless the catalogue explains that reuse.

`ObligationFulfillmentVerifierPort::verify_pair` and `WaiverVerifierPort::verify_pair` are synchronous `&self` methods even though both docs describe dispatching to LLM capabilities. That hides blocking external I/O behind a sync boundary without any justification in the catalogue; make the ports async or explicitly document the blocking choice.

Track-active guard ownership is split across layers. The cli_driver DTOs for derive/check/evaluate say the handler enforces `track/<id>` before translation, while `DeriveTestObligationsCommand` and `CheckTestObligationsCommand` say the interactor rejects on the guard even though `ObligationDeriveError` and `ObligationCheckError` have no `TrackNotActive` variant.
